title: OXO Brew Conical Burr Coffee Grinder , Silver
description:
About this item
Stainless steel conical burrs create uniform grounds for optimal flavor
15 grind size settings (plus additional microsettings) from fine for espresso to coarse for French press and cold brew
One-touch start remembers your last setting, just push to grind
Large-capacity hopper holds up to 3/4 lb/12 oz of coffee beans
UV-blocking tint shields coffee beans from UV rays
Mess-free hopper with “trap door” keeps beans contained when you remove it
Stainless steel static-fighting container significantly reduces static
Powerful DC motor preserves flavor and won’t overheat beans
› See more product details
reviews_5s:
(I am an ex professional barista.)

CONS:

-The grounds container doesn't lock into place and will sometimes vibrate out during grinding. This is the only serious flaw with the product, and I feel it's a minor one. I've gone through many of the reviews and it seems that it's simply a matter of construction inconsistency. Most people's containers "click" into place; a minority do not. I was just unlucky enough to get one of the ones that don't.

-You can't remove the bottom burr to clean it. They really did do their best to make this easy to clean and I appreciate that you don't have to undo a bunch of microscopic screws just to clean your burrs, but I really wish I could remove BOTH burrs to give them a thorough wipe-down. It's difficult to clean the one that's stuck inside the grinder. The other lifts out easily by a cute little handle.

PROS:

-High quality, consistent grind. The brewing methods I use most all hover around the medium grind range, so I haven't really tested the extremes of coarse and fine. Can't speak to those. But as far as the medium ranges, it grinds beautifully and consistently. That's what matters in the end, right?

-The beans feed very well, even for single dosing. Never an issue.

-As mentioned above, the ability to clean the grinder is taken into account in the construction. No need to delicately deconstruct the whole thing and keep track of a bunch of itty bitty screws and springs. The top part of the grinder and the top burr simply turn-and-lift out, and then turn-and-lock back into place. So nice.

-It's aesthetically pleasing and takes up little room on the counter. All the materials have a quality feel.

-It isn't super noisy. All grinders are gonna make noise, to be sure, but as far as grinders go, this one has a pretty gentle sound. I've definitely used my fair share of grinders that made me feel like my brain was going to vibrate out of my skull, and this one has a polite hum by comparison.

-The price for this level of quality is unbeatable. I can't even believe I paid less than one hundred dollars for this. Real talk, folks: these are steel conical burrs. Solid construction. 40+ grind settings. Did I mention steel conical burrs? I never thought I would own something like this for less than $250. You cannot beat this price point/quality intersection. You just can't. This grinder is price-meets-quality king.

USAGE:

You're working with three variables: time, grind, and amount. There are two popular approaches to working out your dose.

Method 1: You leave 'amount' as the open variable. With this method, you dump all your beans in the hopper and store them there. You then adjust grind and time until you're getting the right dose at the right grind level.

Method 2: You leave 'time' as the open variable. With this method, you only deposit the amount of beans you plan to use for each dose, adjust the grind as needed, and let it take whatever amount of time it takes. You're adjusting the amount and the grind, rather than adjusting the grind and the time. (This is called "single dosing.")

Go to any coffee forum, and you'll be pages of debate about which of these methods is superior. Honestly, you should use the method that feels best for YOU.

The reason I bring it up here is because people seem anxious that Method #2 will damage the burrs over time, since you run them all the way to empty every time you grind.

Here's my take: I use Method #2, because I feel that the beans start to taste stale if left in the hopper. (Everyone's tastebuds are different; there's no right or wrong.) This means that I let the burrs run until I hear the sound change from a low growl to a high pitched growl, which indicates that the burrs are grinding empty, and then I manually stop the grind.

I honestly don't see any issue with this, and I don't feel any anxiety about it. Think about it: if you're cleaning the burrs between bean swaps, you're letting them run for several seconds on empty anyway. Even the manufacturer instructions tell you to do this when cleaning the burrs! The only difference here is that instead of intentionally running them on empty for several seconds to clean them, you're running them on empty for one single second every day/dose. I'd never recommend doing that on a fine espresso setting, but as long as you're in the medium-to-coarse range, I don't see any possible ways the burrs could damage each other. There's no way the burrs are touching at that distance, regardless of variables like heat expanding the metal and other things coffee nerds like to debate about.

I hope this review was helpful. I'll update in a year to let you know if this grinder held up through daily use.This checks all the boxes. We grind our own coffee every morning for a fresh cup. While there are many coffee grinders that do a good job, most that do are quite expensive. And those that are more reasonably priced often are not very consistent in their grind. But this oxo grinder checks all the boxes. Its price is very reasonable, only $89. And the grind quality is very consistent, no matter whether you need a coarse grind, fine grind, or something in between. It comes out well every time. It has a stainless steel container, so no plastic container with grinds sticking to the sides, it empties out every time. The reservoir holds about 10 or 12 ounces of beans, and is shaded so it keeps the beans from too much light. You just turn the reservoir to the grind you prefer. It has a dial that you just turn to set the timer to grind the amount you’ll need very easy to clean, you reach in, turn the spindle to unlock the reservoir which closes off the bottom so no beans spill out, lift it up, then grab the bail on the inner grinder turn it counterclockwise and lift it out to clean everything out. A very nice grinder that we can highly recommend.I rarely do product reviews. However, every once in a while I buy something so good … or so bad that I feel like I have to make everyone aware of my situation. When I buy a new gadget, I’m that guy that spends all evening after work researching it and I use multiple points of reference - Google, Reddit, Amazon reviews … I spend hours reading Amazon reviews. And it doesn’t matter if I’m looking to buy new measuring cups or a new washing machine, the process is the same - multiple evenings of tireless research.

Now about my coffee addiction. I wouldn’t say that I’m a coffee snob per se. But I’m definitely a Starbucks guy - not a Folgers guy. And I drink coffee daily with an almost religious conviction. Multiple cups.

About a year ago, a buddy of mine lost his job and took a bridge gig working at Starbucks as a barista. It definitely elevated his coffee game well beyond the Average Joe (pun intended). But what was most impressive was his newly found skill of making French Press Coffee. After my first cup, I was instantly hooked and on a quest to recreate this manna.

I quickly learned that the real secret sauce wasn’t the French press manufacturer, it wasn’t the filtered water, it wasn’t the pinch of Kosher salt; it’s using fresh whole coffee beans and getting the perfect coarse grind.

Start the research! So, going into this I was thinking one night of research … maybe two max. But my gawd is the coffee drinking community an optioned and fickle lot. And it didn’t matter if it was a 15 bar espresso machine master, a drip coffee guru, or a seasoned French presser; no one agrees on grind size or the machine that will get you there! It turned out to be a tougher than expected mission but after about a week of research, I felt that I could distill my choice down to the OXO Conical Brew Coffee Grinder for the following reasons. The reviews … for a French press coffee course grind … were pretty exceptional. The price was super reasonable. The conical burr design was probably the only thing everyone agreed on. And although my OXO experience is limited to a few spatulas and a can opener, it is a household name that I am familiar with.

Now the results. This thing is absolutely amazing. I use Setting 15. As previously mentioned, no one is going to agree on grind size. But for me Setting 15 is where it’s at for the French press technique. I’ve gotten a consistent grind similar to fresh ground coarse pepper … again subjective. It’s not too loud during the grind cycle but it’s an electric motor powered mechanical grinder so don’t expect it to be noiseless. The grounds container snaps into the grinder base and stays firmly attached when in use. The lid on the grounds container keeps things from flying all over the place and the container itself is easy to detach and attach and makes pouring the grinds into your press a breeze. I really like this grinder.

So, if you’ve read this far and you’re still on the fence … hop on off and click Buy Now. You won’t be disappointed … at least not if French Press Coffee is your jam.

NOTE: I have not disassembled the grinder for cleaning yet so I can’t comment on that process. However, I can’t imagine it’s overly complicated because everything about this machine is incredibly user friendly.After reading a lot of reviews and noticing the people who are complaining, maybe trying to take this grinder to its maximum level of fine powder grind like Turkish coffee.

I use this machine daily and grind up to four espresso shots every day for the last year and a half. We discovered that if you Take a little time and figure out how long you have to leave the timer on you can make an exact amount of grinds perfectly for each time you use your machine. Every cup of espresso is fresh!

We leave our beans in the machine because it’s empty every five days so we don’t believe that the beans are stale and the coffee taste delicious.

You could leave the grinder on timer unlimited, and then pour in the beans you want to grind, but imagine having a car running, and you throw a bunch of marbles into the engine. Those birds in the grinder are gonna take a little shock when you throw beans in there. And yeah, that might gum things up. When it’s full and the beans are already there it’s easier for the machine to just keep grinding! For those that like to take it all apart and clean it every day and I’m worried about their grinder not working properly, we’ve had no issue and I’ve just used the machine for a year now would never cleaning the birds at all.

It just works perfect every time.

It’s interesting that if you just move the line above or back a little bit on the timer, you may or may not get the exact amount to make a perfect espresso shot so watch what you’re doing when you push the on off button because if you turn your finger, you might increase or decrease the time. Other than that, it’s a fantastic machine!

For all those people that are hooting and hollering that it’s not as good as a $200 machine, I wouldn’t know because I won’t spend $200 on a grinder.

And for all those that are dissatisfied that it’s not as good or better than a $50 machine when I hear ya because a $50 machine is 50 bucks And you’d hoped that a $50 machine would work good. But this machine for the price we paid is absolutely fantastic.

I’ve also heard some people say that there didn’t click in and lock in for those folks. I say I’m sorry and why didn’t you return it as soon as it got in and it didn’t work perfect? As a matter fact for anyone is complaining, why didn’t you return it as soon as it didn’t work properly? Seems as though 9099% of the rest of the people who purchase this Had an excellent machine.

And for those that got a machine was built on a Monday or a Friday where the folks were either ready to go home Friday or too tired on a Monday, well if your machine doesn’t work, you should return it.

Everyone should be purchasing things with some kind of credit card that would give them an extra #Warranty, and of course you know that you could always just reverse the charges if it doesn’t work right within the first 90 days.I've had my share of coffee grinders over the years. From the one button manual blade-type, to several burr-type. This is, by far, the quietest and easiest to use, almost.

The MOST impressive part about this grinder is how quiet it is. I can now grind coffee before 7:00 AM without worry of waking my partner up. The lack of sound doesn't take away from its performance. I find the grinds to be much more consistent that others I've used, as well as the fact it does not rev with a higher pitch when the beans have depleted in the hopper.

The fact they use stainless steel for the grind collection is brilliant. I have another grinder at work that is a plastic static magnet and requires cleanup with every use. A simple tap and all the grinds fall out with no clean up. The difference in use is night and day.

The grind selector is ideal. A medium grind provides a well balanced brew in my drip coffee maker.

The only downside is the cup / quantity selector. It's trial-and-error. Neither the dial nor manual give clear indication how much the grinder will provide. I have a 5-cup coffee maker and prefer one tsp per cup. It has taken me several grinds to find the ideal amount.

For what it's worth, I think this grinder should have much better reviews from both professional critics and home users.This is a pretty excellent addition to my morning routine. Oxo is, in my experience, a company that makes high quality products and this is no exception. A few things I like about it:
- It is really solid, I can tell it's well made from quality parts. Even the plastic parts seem good
- The stainless steel grounds holder is a game-changer. I hated the static build-up when using my plastic Capresso, with this unit I can seamlessly empty the grounds into my pour-over filter, no need to get the brush out.
- Setting the coarseness of the grind is super-simple and actually results in what I'm expecting - from fine to coarse
- It's pretty quiet compared to my Capresso, I don't need to worry about annoying my neighbors

Although it's only been a week I can safely say that as long as it doesn't have some major malfunction this will be my go-to grinder for the long term. Highly recommended.Consistently grinds the perfect coffee for pour-overs. Once you find the perfect grind, and the amount dialed in (took me a few cups), it's a consistently perfect cup of coffee every time. I have used a spice grinder, and a travel/portable conical burr grinder - but have found my Nirvana with this. I drink pour-overs during the morning and make French Press coffee on the weekends, and this thing gives you the ultimate grind for each brew type. All this in a tidy small, sleek profile.

So easy to put an entire bag in the UV protected hopper once a week, instead of pulling the beans out of the bag multiple times a day. Oh, and yes, there is static unless you mist your beans prior to grinding.Got this to replace a 10 year old Cuisinart grinder that finally quit on me and was hard to clean. A lot of thought was put into the design of this one that convince me to buy it over another Cuisinart and I'm very happy I did. The directions as you open the packaging are designed for folks who otherwise wouldn't bother reading them which I thought was cute and useful. This is so much quieter to run, has a timer setting for the grinding instead of volume setting, so you know how long it's going to make noise for in case you are on a conference call you can only briefly mute when using it. It's much easier to take apart to clean. The metal hopper has a soft plastic lid that doesn't need to be taken off to empty it, making it faster to use. (I previously dropped and broke the hard brittle plastic lid on my Cuisinart grinder hopper and had to super glue it back to get it to run.) All in all I'm glad a spent a little more for this one instead of going with a new one of the grinder I had before.Get it! This burr grinder does an excellent job for course grinding. (I haven't used it for fine grinding.) It's easy to clean the external burr and you would use a grinder cleaner for the internal parts. Removing the bin is easy to do in order to get to the external burr. Taking the burr off takes some getting use to, but it becomes easy once you do it a couple of times. You do have to take coffee bin off to change the grind numbers, but it's not a big deal. It's also easy to adjust the grind time. You can grind a lot of coffee in it, but it doesn't take up a lot of room. The only minor issue I have with it is getting the bin back on, but maybe that's user error!This OXO grinder has been working well for me for almost a full year. I purchased this grinder as my first step in improving my coffee game and trying to perfect my pour-over technique. The consistency of the grind size is very good, and the ability to easily adjust the coarseness means this works well for both my pour over and preparing cold brew.

Good value electric burr grinder for the price, and OXO generally produces some solid kitchen equipment.

To be as blunt and simple as possible, the OXO BREW Conical Burr Grinder is the worst product I have ever purchased online through Amazon. Furthermore, my wife has been in contact via email with OXO's customer support team about the poor quality of this product, and their support team refuses to either refund or replace the product. We have provided them with both videos and photos showing that the unit functions either very poorly or does not function at all without lots of troubleshooting. Yet, their engineers have responded saying that the unit appears to be functioning "normally" in the videos (one of which I will attach to this review). However, at this point the unit does not work without quite a bit of frustration--plugging and unplugging multiple times or sweeping out the burrs multiple times just to grind enough beans for a pour over coffee. Even though I have only owned this unit for one month, I see no other solution than to place this unit in the trash and buy a more expensive unit from another manufacturer. I am an avid home coffee brewer, and I have owned other coffee products from Bonavita, Hario, Mr. Coffee, Cuisinart, and OXO. I can say unequivocally, this OXO burr grinder is the worst coffee product I have ever owned or purchased. I will attach video and photographic proof that the unit does not work correctly and will explain further below the problems with the unit.

Initially, the unit worked great. For the first week, the unit produced a reliable and consistent grind of Trader Joe's Ethiopian beans (~$8.99 a bag). Then, the trouble started the second week when I began grinding Stumptown Hair Bender beans (~$15.99 a bag). The unit jammed mid-cycle for the first time. The button on the front of the unit would not start the motor so I tried troubleshooting the unit in multiple ways, following the instructions in the owner's manual. I unplugged it and plugged it back in--start button still did not work. I opened the bean hopper and nothing appeared jammed. So finally I opened up the burrs and swept them out. When I put the unit back together, it worked, and I thought the problem was solved. However, over the next week, the unit kept jamming every time I used it with the Stumptown beans. Sometimes it would jam multiple times in a row. Each time I had to open the unit and sweep out the burrs to get it to work. This process, while being extremely frustrating and time-consuming, also caused the unit to produce an inconsistent grind size. I've attached a picture showing that I get chunks of beans in my pour over because I have to play an elaborate game with the machine just to get it to function. For a unit that regularly retails for around $100, this is absolutely unacceptable for a new product. Furthermore, if a $100 burr grinder cannot be used on a premium product like Stumptown, then that grinder is entirely worthless to coffee enthusiasts.

After I finished the bag of Stumptown coffee, I tried the grinder again on the Trader Joe's beans (since those beans had initially worked well with the unit). Now, I began experiencing the same problems with Trader Joe's. In order to grind 5 scoops of beans for one large pour over coffee, I had to either: (1) Open and sweep the burrs multiple times or (2) Plug and unplug the unit multiple times because it grinds for about 3 seconds before jamming even when the timer is set on 30 seconds. I have attached a video showing the unit functioning in this way. In the video, you will see the game I have to play just to grind beans using a unit that was purchased only 3 weeks prior.

Here's my personal thought regarding the performance issues of the machine. I assume the motor has a fail-safe feature designed to stop the motor in event that it becomes clogged. This would prevent the motor from being damaged if a very small stone or an extremely hard bean got stuck in the burrs (which can happen on a rare occasion). My guess is that this setting isn't quite right in my unit and that the unit stops every time there is the tiniest bit of resistance on the motor. This would explain why I have to unplug the unit multiple times just to completely grind a cup of beans. Either way, it is entirely unreasonable for OXO to expect users to have to troubleshoot a new unit with such frequency as a part of the unit's "normal" functioning.

Currently, OXO does not want to address my concerns with this unit so I have decided to place this negative review. I've never felt compelled before to write a negative review on Amazon. Hopefully, they will decide to improve the product and respond to customer concerns. At this point, I cannot recommend this product to any other buyer, and I will no longer purchase any kitchen or coffee products manufactured by OXO. Finally, I've decided I don't even want a replacement for this unit. Even if OXO offered to replace it, I would refuse. That alone shows my level of disappointment with the product. The overall build quality feels cheap to me, especially the timer and start button on the front. I owned an entry-level Mr. Coffee burr grinder (~$30) for 7 years that "felt" better--button quality, weight of product, sound of motor, etc. If OXO decides to respond to my concerns, I will only accept a full refund for the purchase price of the product so that I can purchase another unit from a different manufacturer.

UPDATE: OXO finally agreed to refund us the purchase price of the unit after I posted this negative review and video on Amazon. The refund process took some time, but we did eventually get a check in the mail for the full purchase price of the unit. We will explore other options for a replacement unit.I bought this OXO coffee grinder for my brand spankin’ new kitchen. My first kitchen in my first house that I own. Which is all very dramatic and fraught and it’s all amazing. I love this kitchen so much. On top of all of this, I’m a chef and baker by trade. I have been for 16 years. I add this to say I am particular. Absolutely. It comes w the territory. I have been drinking La Colombe Corsica for about 20 years. There are a few others I drink too but 99% of the coffee I drink is La Colombe Corsica every damn day. The Corsica is a dark, oily French/Italian roast kind of roast. I had no idea this grinder was not supposed to accommodate that style of coffee bean until I read some of the see other reviews looking for experiences like my own.

The first one of these grinders I received from Amazon worked for literally 12 seconds. It ground maybe a tablespoon of beans and shorted. Done. Game over. No more brand new coffee grinder.

I called Amazon (which I get to do all the time now a my renovation. We’re basically bffs.) and they shipped a replacement. So far, no issues w the grinding operation. It’s been maybe a month?

My issues and the reasons I came here to write a review are these. The coffee tastes bizarre. As I said, I’ve been drinking this same coffee for 20 years. I know what this coffee tastes like and I *L O V E* the way this coffee tastes. I have experimented w different coarsenesses and ratios of those coarsenesses. The way this grinder is grinding the beans completely and utterly distorts the taste of my coffee. It’s heartbreaking to me that pounds of this coffee are getting pulverized; losing any semblance of their magnificence. So much so, I went back to my Cuisinart little job that I have to put two separate batches into this morning (which is the reason I got the OXO grinder in the first place).

Also, what I’m not seeing mentioned is the container the grounds go into makes AN ENORMOUS mess. There are grounds all over my brand new counters (did I mention I have a new kitchen?), the tray I hold my coffee station on, the floor underneath the counters and coffee station. It’s a major deal.

A friend who owns a series of super cool coffee shops in Oregon where they often serve that new, trendy, lightly roasted roast, not the the stuff I like where you get punched in the face w coffee flavor, told me grinders w new blades often change the flavor of the coffee when they’re new. He went into the science of it which I’ll spare you. I gotta say though, it’s never happened to me before w a new grinder and I’ve been drinking coffee now for almost 30 years.

I’m not a coffee nerd, I’m not a barista or a former pro, but I am a food professional w a pretty sensitive palate who hates the world at 6am when she drinks her beloved La Colombe and it tastes like a completely foreign and unpleasant hot, brown liquid.

I’ll probably give it another week of experimentation, but the mess alone is enough for me to explore other options let alone the bad taste. If you do a better job than I did and actually read these reviews instead of simply going w « Number 1 bestseller on Amazon! », I’d advise you to keep looking.I wish I could write a good review of this product because there is a lot to like about it.
I used it to replace a Bodum grinder that I had for 30 years.
The features are great. The problem is that it clogs way too easily.
I have to do my dark roast beans (not particularly oily) on somewhere between medium to coarse to keep it from clogging. This is way coarser than I want for my automatic machine. Nowhere remotely near an espresso grind; more like a french press grind.

Here's what Oxo support has to say about the issue:
"the most common issue we help resolve is clogs, please follow the steps below"
Of course, the issue isn't that you can't resolve the clog, it's that you have to do it frequently despite grinding the coffee much coarser than you really want.

FWIW, here are the steps:
Unplug machine
Remove, empty and wipe down hopper
Remove upper burr by lifting metal handle and turning to left, brush off grinds with a soft flexible brush and remove any debris from under the upper burr. You should be able to see the grey color of the area under the upper burr if all debris has been removed.
Use a large paper clip or a pipe cleaner to clean the chute that the grinds go thru to get in the container from the bottom opening. There is a slight curve, so you need to push up and wiggle the paperclip to remove the clog.
Put parts back together and see if issue is resolved.This product worked erratically initially and then stopped working altogether within seven months. The two-year warranty is ineffectual since this is how OXO Customer Service attempts to turn you into its repair person after being informed that you have already spent an hour on the instruction manual's troubleshooting steps:

"Remove, empty and wipe down hopper

Remove upper burr by lifting metal handle and turning to left, brush off grinds with a soft flexible brush and remove any debris from under the upper burr. You should be able to see the grey color of the area under the upper burr if all debris has been removed.

Be sure to use a 4- to 8-inch-long flexible style brush to clean the chute. Something like a straw cleaning brush, pipe cleaners or a large paper clip. You would wiggle this up into the chute from the bottom, wiggle it around to get past the curve. Once the chute is clear, you will see the wire or brush come out at the top where beans are ground. Once the chute is clear, you may be able to use Grindz tablets that are made to clean grinders.

Use a large paper clip or a pipe cleaner to clean the chute that the grinds go thru to get in the container from the bottom opening. There is a slight curve, so you need to push up and wiggle the paperclip to remove the clog.

Put parts back together and see if issue is resolved."

If these fix-it-yourself instructions don't work, OXO Customer Service tells you to provide the serial number and a "Picture of the tools used to clean the grounds chute and burr ring;" and "A short video of the issue."

If OXO's way of dealing with an inoperative coffee grinder seems like a problem to you, you might want to consider a different manufacturer.Get your tools out….

I’ve purchased this grinder twice. My bad. When it works it works well. But not for long. Both grinders I’ve had work great until coffee jams up and clogs The internals requiring you to empty the hopper…remove the hopper, unscrew machine screw holding burr assembly, twist out the top of burr mechanism, remove main burr grinder while being careful not to lose the 3 centimeter long pins under the burr…. Bang and clean and use a flat head screw driver to clear the clogged coffee from within main core and also underneath at the spout where grounds come out.

Reassemble everything and….using needle nose pliers carefully reseat the 3 pins if you haven’t lost them into machine or elsewhere and it may work again until the next clog. I’m done doing this. There’s a reason why this grinder is no longer at the top of recommended burr grinders…yet still one of the most expensive Buy at your own discretion. Also this second unit I bought was far and away louder the first one. Why???Been eyeing this grinder for a couple features, most importantly the hopper size. Says holds 12 oz. it does not. We went so far as to purchase a 6 pack of 12 oz. bags of Starbucks Sumatra expecting to dump an entire bag into the hopper. No joy, only holds about 10-11 ounces, not a whole bag. So no more convenient than our Cuisinart. The Starbucks coffee is so-so, more on that in another review. Wont buy again. 12 ounce bags very are a popular size albeit not the most economical.
Next: says is static free, it is not. See pic. This was shot holding the cup horizontally. Coffee is stuck to the top.
But worst thing: full grind cycle press produces exactly 40 grams, half what we need for a full pot. I don't like to measure beans or water. We use a Zojirushi EC YGC120 which has a removable reservoir. Easy to fill to the same level every time. I want a grinder that produces the same amount of coffee every time: 70g, 80g, 90g or whatever we determine is the best for that particular bean. So a grinder that maxes out at 40 grams per cycle is no bueno and making a half a pot at a time, also no good.
Will be returningProduct arrived and worked to expectation for 2-3 grinds then it ran but with no grounds. Took apart cleared and reassembled. Ran 2-3 times then again, no grounds. Sense a pattern emerging? Took apart cleaned and then examined the mechanism. There is a cheap plastic sleeve with a very shallow (too shallow) plastic indent slide lock which really is nothing more than a pressure fit which just will not stand up to the task of grinding coffee. Then the feed from the bottom of the grinder to the receptacle is not a clean clear path so not really sure how the beans are conveyed from the grinder to the container. One would think that you could easily see light if held at the right angle as it should be a fairly straight path given putting in an angle makes for it not maybe working so well. Oh, hey that is exactly what seems to be happening. I cannot tell if the path is blocked or if the top burr is popping free thus not feeding the coffee into the bottom burr or BOTH. but either way I am done struggling with this concraption. And to add insult to injury to return you have to go through Oxo, you can't just process through Amazon. Unfortunately, it is past business hours so I do not know how that will go but I will be sure to post. Not quite sure if I got one that was just assembled wrong at the factory or if it is really just poorly designed. I have been happy with all my other previous Oxo products but they were all manual so maybe electric appliances are not to be included in with those other quality Oxo products. I was really surprised and disappointed to see the poorly engineered shallow plastic locking mechanism but I suspect that is not the only design flaw seeing as I cannot see through or figure out how to check to see that the feed path to the container is clear. I had a Shardor with a steel (not conical) burr grinder that worked flawlessly for 2 years until I wore the burrs out. That is no longer available so I thought I would step up to the big leagues.This grinder does a phenomenal job of grinding coffee and for that I have no complaints. I bought this grinder to improve the espressos I was making for my wife. For that I am using a fine grind. My guess is this would be less of an issue you are using a medium or courser grind.

For that the grind definitely performed the enhancement I was hoping for. In addition, the stainless-steel canister is great and does not collect static electricity, so the coffee does not stick to it. The problem is the chute the coffe comes out of is plastic and is relatively long. As a result the coffee consistently sticks to it and will clog. The picture included is after 2 grinds of 18 seconds each, 36 seconds in total. You can see that the coffee is starting to build up in the chute. By day 5 this will become clogged, and I will need to clean it out. In order to do this, I take it completely apart to include the top burr. I then use my air compressor to blow it out clean. Needless to say, this is an incredibly messy process. It does not matter what type I have used whether fresh roast or an older roast. My hope was I could place the portafilter directly under the chute, but that seems to clog it faster so I no longer do that.

Outside of this one issue I would give it five stars, but the clogging is such an inconvenience and a messy process that I feel 1 star is most appropriate. All of this could be avoided if they would either shorten the shoot, use stainless steel for the shot or both. as is I would not recommend this product if you are going to use it for fine grinds.When I first bought this grinder in Feb 2024, it was great. I played with the timer for it to grind up just the right amount of beans to make the pot of coffee my wife and I like. After around 6 months, I noticed the grinds coming out great for the first burst during the grind, but they very, very little the rest of the grind time. I've cleaned the grinder thoroughly at least twice a month since getting it to avoid this issue. Being under warranty, I tried contacting OXO customer service and received an email of how to troubleshoot. The troubleshooting steps were the same steps (basically thoroughly cleaning like I've always done) that I tried doing multiple times before contacting customer service. When it didn't work, they asked for pictures of the tools I used and video of the issue. I sent them this information and haven't heard anything back.

There's not really a point to pay $100 for a nice grinder with a timer if the timer is not reliable. Save your money and look at something else. I regret this purchase and wish I'd have spent double the money on another option. A friend has has the Breville and it has been a champ for him for over 3 years now....this OXO unit is a let down.When I received this, I read the manual. It says it does not work well with dark oily beans. I should have returned it right there. Is there another reason someone buys a coffee grinder?

It worked ok the first dozen times or so, but even at the maximum grind size the kernels are significantly smaller than is recommended for Cold Brew. I used it anyway. Your coffee will be stronger and have more grounds in it, but I like strong coffee, so that was ok (dark oily beans are my favorite).

The trouble came when the machine started clogging. It is not very easy to clean. The output slot is way too small, and the area behind it is way too large. There will be a substantial amount of grounds plugging the machine, all of which need to be thrown away. When your machine stops delivering grounds to the hopper, that is what is going on.

Cleaning the cones is no easy task. The manual says to turn the inside cone counterclockwise. That is easier said than done when the machine is plugged. I almost broke my channel locks. Finally, it turned before anything broke, and I was able to remove it. You will need another person to hold the machine while you are doing this. Don't let them hurt their wrist (yes, that happened)!

It is back working, for now. I would spend twice as much to get a better machine, but now I need to finish breaking this one before I can justify the expense.
